# iliad-010 — review, pass 1 (Iliad 2.278–368)

Pass 1 covers `units.json` only; `gloss.json` is read in pass 2. Method: notes first (every grammatical label, positional claim and cross-reference checked against the line and, for cross-references, against `source/iliad-monro-allen1920.json`); then Greek to `l` word by word; `l` against `i`; remembered English in `i`; quotation marks; the flagged line by hand. Edits were made by script on `units.json` only; the `t` of all 49 units is byte-identical before and after. `new-renderings.md` needed no change (no rendering listed there was altered; the one `l` that departed from a table row, εὐρυάγυιαν, now follows the existing row at 2.141 and so needs no new row).

Totals: 0 high, 5 medium, 19 low (24 edits, on 21 fields).

## Checked and found sound (no change)

Cross-references verified against the source: 1.73, 1.253, 2.78 (the ὅ σφιν ἐὺ φρονέων line); 2.101 (ἔστη σκῆπτρον ἔχων, Agamemnon); 2.113 (the Ἴλιον ἐκπέρσαντ’ line, published in iliad-008 as ln 112); 2.166–181 (Athena sends Odysseus); 2.185–186 (the sceptre); 2.272–277 (the soldiers' praise, ending iliad-009); 1.69–72 (Calchas); 1.528 (the nod); 1.408; 1.530; 309 and 324 (Olympian, Zeus named); 285 (ἐλέγχιστον); 293 (ἀσχαλάᾳ); 313 and 317 (repeated lines); 336 (ἱππότα); 362 (Ἀγάμεμνον); 365 (γνώσῃ); 369 (Agamemnon answers); Odyssey 12.391–392 (odyssey-061, the μῆχος line). Units 3, 29 and 30 are identical in `l` and `i` to the published iliad-001/-003/-007 and odyssey-090 units; the line 288 wording agrees with iliad-008 as far as the sentence allows. The English for φόνον καὶ κῆρα φέροντες agrees with odyssey-016 and -038 ("slaughter and doom").

Quotation marks: iliad-009 closes the soldiers' speech with ” at 2.277, so this part opens outside any speech (278–283). Odysseus: “ on 284, mark "Odysseus speaks"; the nested Calchas speech opens with ‘ on 323 (mark set, note says why) and closes with ’ at the end of 329 (unit at 326); Odysseus resumes unopened (330, 330) and closes with ” at the end of 332 (unit at 331); the army and Nestor's introduction (333–336) sit outside; Nestor: “ on 337, mark "Nestor speaks", ” at the end of 368 (unit at 367), in both layers; no speech runs on into iliad-011. Counts, `l` and `i` alike: 2 “, 2 ”, 1 ‘, 1 closing ’ (unit 326; the other ’ are apostrophes). Paragraph marks `p` fall on 278 and 333 as the packet shows. `l` and `t` have the same line count in every unit; `ln` is the first line of each unit.

Hand scan of 337, ὦ πόποι ἦ δὴ παισὶν ἐοικότες ἀγοράασθε: ὦ πό-ποι | ἦ δὴ | παι-σὶν ἐ- | οι-κό-τες | ἀ-γο-ρά- | ασ-θε. Foot 1 is a dactyl only if ποι is short before ἦ (correption); feet 3 and 4 are dactyls (ἐο- not in synizesis); foot 5 needs the first α of ἀγοράασθε, short by nature, to count long (ἀ– γο⏑ ρά⏑), then ασ-θε closes the line. That is 16 syllables and six feet, and it agrees with the scanner's second reading. The irregularity is real and the note (ln 337) already says it in one sentence: ποι shortened before ἦ, and ἀ lengthened in the fifth foot. No change needed.

## Considered and refused

- **κῆρα as "doom" (350):** the table reserves "doom" for πότμος, but odyssey-016 (271) and odyssey-038 (511) ship "slaughter and doom" for this very phrase, φόνον καὶ κῆρα φέροντες. Kept, since Odyssey formulae are reused; 359 has πότμον "doom" too, and the two words are told apart by the reader's context and by θάνατον beside πότμον there.
- **"ἐλεεινά" attached to cheeping in `i` but to devouring in `l` (314):** the Greek is ambiguous and the note says so and says the English puts it with the cheeping; `l` order follows the Greek.
- **"hold to your unshaken plan as before" for σὺ δ’ ἔθ’ ὡς πρὶν ἔχων ἀστεμφέα βουλήν (344, `i`):** makes the participle ἔχων an imperative. Considered as a change of force, refused because the sense (keep to the plan, and lead) is the sentence's sense and the note lays out the participle.
- **"childish creatures" (337, `i`) for νηπιάχοις:** "creatures" is an addition, but it only gives the adjective a noun, as `l` does with "ones"; refused.
- **"though we have been here so long" (342, `i`):** the concessive "though" is the English's reading of a bare participle, within what πολὺν χρόνον ἐνθάδ’ ἐόντες allows; refused.
- **"strivings" for ὁρμήματα (356):** might be remembered from a published translation. Rebuilt from ὁρμή "rush, impulse" with the result-noun ending, it is the obvious noun, and the rendering is already fixed in `new-renderings.md` with the alternatives turned down for stated reasons. Kept.
- **"Why ever" for τίπτε (323, `l`):** the Odyssey ships "Why ever" in `l` for τίπτε at 8.363 and 3.225 and plain "Why" elsewhere; `l` keeps ποτε. Kept.
- **"the sons of the Achaeans" / "the first and the last" order in 281 `i`:** reordered but all words kept; refused.
- **Dropped μέν in 324 and δέ-connectives in a few `l` lines:** `l` leaves μέν unrendered throughout the published parts; refused.
- **ἴαχον called "unaugmented aorist" (333):** the form has no augment and is an aorist/imperfect in the grammars; refused as a quibble.
- **ἄρχευ’ as "imperative of ἄρχω" (344):** the exact formation is debated; the label gives the right meaning and the right mood. Refused.
- **"θεῶν" ambiguity (321):** note already gives both attachments; refused.
- **"ἄναξ … vocative" (284, 360):** ἄναξ serves as nominative and vocative; true as labelled.
- **Remembered English:** no `i` phrase found that arrives whole from a modern translation and cannot be rebuilt from the grammar. Nearest: 299 "stay a while, until we learn", 306 "complete hecatombs" and 356 "strivings and groans"; each follows the Greek word for word and the table, so none was changed.
- **Metre of lines other than 337:** the packet flags none; not scanned further.

# iliad-010 — review, pass 2

Method: units re-read independently (notes first, then Greek to `l`, `l` to `i`, quotation marks, house renderings against both tables); `gloss.json` read in full, every parse of the 216 novel forms checked against the line and against the unit's `l`, `i` and note; the 17 `__broaden__` entries checked to keep the old entry (from `iliad-glossary.json`) whole, and the 249 known forms checked for use not covered by the existing entry. Quotation marks re-counted (2 “, 2 ”, 1 ‘, one closing ’ at the end of the unit at 326, in `l` and `i`): sound.

## Gloss checks: parses confirmed against the line (no change)

The six forms the glosser flagged: ἀμφεποτᾶτο (impf. 3 sg. of ἀμφιποτάομαι, contracted -ᾶτο; subject μήτηρ; agrees with note); ἐπέπιθμεν (plpf. 1 pl. of πέποιθα, ‘we trusted’; agrees with `l`/`i` and note); ἀσχαλάᾳ / ἀσχαλάαν (3 sg. and inf. with diectasis, as in the note). Also checked and sound: εἰλέωσιν (subj. 3 pl., general relative with ὅν … περ), ὑπέσταν, ἀγοράασθε (2 pl.), ἑσταότες, ὑποπεπτηῶτες, τετριγῶτας, ἐλελιξάμενος, θέμεναι, εὑρέμεναι, γνώμεναι, ἐπιφρασσαίατο, ἠγερέθοντο, ἧς (292, 357 possessive; the broaden keeps the old relative entry whole), ᾗς (341 relative fem. dat. pl.; broaden keeps the old possessive entry whole), κεῖνος, τὼς, ἄνεῳ, κομόωντες. All 17 old `__broaden__` entries begin with the old entry whole and add readings the part needs (αὐτῶν, κατά, οἷς, πολὺν, νῶτα, τῷ, ὅ, εἰς, ἧς, ᾗς, ἦ, ὑπὸ, ὑπ, περὶ, ὡς, ἐνθάδε, φίλα); four more broaden entries were added in this pass (δ, τόν, ἐπὶ, ἢ) and ὅ and περὶ were amended.

## Considered and refused

- **ἐκτελέουσιν as present in `l`/`i` (286):** both readings are in the note and gloss; the English takes the present. Kept.
- **"hold to your unshaken plan" (344, `i`):** pass 1 refusal stands (sense of the sentence is kept; ἔχων is laid out in the note).
- **κατήσθιε "without the final -ν" (319 note and gloss):** harmless, true (movable ν absent); kept.
- **ἴαχον "impf." in gloss against "unaugmented aorist" in the note:** the form is both in the grammars; kept (as pass 1).
- **κατακοιμάομαι (gloss) against κατακοιμάω (note):** the gloss lemmatises the deponent used in the passive aorist; compatible. Kept.
- **εἰδομένη "having made herself like" (279):** follows the table row for ἐεισάμενος; kept.
- **ἀνώγει "was bidding" in the gloss against "bade":** gloss gives the tense value of the pluperfect-imperfect form, `l` the narrative English. Kept.
- **"Zeus the counsellor has shown" (324, `i`) for aorist ἔφηνε:** present-perfect English for a speech about a continuing sign; matches the house phrase in iliad-009. Kept.
